extraction.name: CT-RATE
extraction.description: A public open-source dataset of paired non-contrast 3D chest CT volumes and corresponding radiology text reports, with abnormality labels extracted from reports.

extraction.rai:dataCollection: Chest CT volumes and corresponding radiology reports were curated from Istanbul Medipol University Mega Hospital; reports and metadata were anonymized, reports were translated from Turkish to English and reviewed by bilingual medical students, non-chest or contrast volumes were excluded, and every reconstructed chest volume from the hospital database was incorporated.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Non-contrast chest CT volumes, radiology text reports, and metadata from Istanbul Medipol University Mega Hospital hospital database.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Reports were anonymized by removing personal information, translated from Turkish to English using Google Translate API, and reviewed and corrected by bilingual final-year medical students; CT volumes with contrast material or body parts other than the chest were excluded; orientation was standardized; metadata was anonymized; volumes were resized to uniform spacing, center-cropped or padded to a fixed resolution, converted to Hounsfield Units, clipped to [-1000, 1000], and normalized to [-1, 1] during training.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Each CT exam is paired with a radiologist-authored report; for abnormality labels, 1,000 reports were manually annotated for 18 abnormalities by merging findings and impression sections, then a RadBERT-RoBERTa-4m model was finetuned and applied to classify the remaining reports; organ-level anatomical segmentation labels were generated using a state-of-the-art segmentation model.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The annotated reports were split into training and validation sets, and the automated report classifier's precision, recall, and F1 scores were reported.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Bilingual final-year medical students reviewed and corrected all translations.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset and models are intended to support future innovations in medical AI and improved patient care, but substantial progress is still needed for clinical deployment.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset is single-institution and from a single geographic and clinical setting, which may bias self-supervised training and limit generalizability to other populations.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset originates from a single institution and geographic setting, which may limit generalizability; CT-CLIP depends on report terminology and prompt choice; CT-CHAT lacks true 3D multimodal baselines for benchmarking; generated reports remain insufficient for clinical use; and the current models are limited to chest CT volumes.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training and internal validation of CT-CLIP and CT-CHAT; zero-shot multi-abnormality detection, finetuning, volume-to-volume retrieval, report-to-volume retrieval, visual question answering, and report generation.

name.evidence: We introduce CT-RATE, a public dataset that pairs 3D medical images with corresponding textual reports.

description.evidence: We curate and open-source CT-RATE, a dataset comprising 25,692 non-contrast 3D chest CT volumes and corresponding radiology text reports from 21,304 unique patients.

url.evidence: Our CT-RATE dataset, comprising paired chest CT volumes and radiology text reports, is publicly accessible via https://huggingface.co/datasets/ibrahimhamamci/CT-RATE [67].

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: Our preprocessing approach, inspired by previous work [20], involved several key steps to standardize all chest CT volumes in the dataset.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: Within CT-RATE, we manually annotate 1,000 reports for 18 distinct abnormalities for this finetuning procedure.

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: The annotated reports are divided into training (80%, 800 reports) and validation (20%, 200 reports) sets.

rai:annotatorDemographics.evidence: Subsequently, these anonymized reports are translated from Turkish to English using the Google Translate API, and bilingual final-year medical students review and correct all translations.

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: Subsequently, these anonymized reports are translated from Turkish to English using the Google Translate API

rai:personalSensitiveInformation.evidence: The patients range in age from 18 to 102 years, with a mean of 48.8 years and a mode of 40 years. The sex distribution is 41.6% female and 58.4% male.

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: Collectively, the open-source release of CT-RATE, CT-CLIP, and CT-CHAT not only addresses critical challenges in 3D medical imaging but also lays the groundwork for future innovations in medical AI and improved patient care.

rai:dataBiases.evidence: First, biases inherent to our single-institution dataset may influence our self-supervised training.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: Despite these advancements, our CT-RATE dataset and the CT-CLIP and CT-CHAT models have certain limitations.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: CT-RATE is divided into training and internal validation sets for experiments (see creating the CT-RATE dataset section of Methods).
